title: Determinant lines are multiplicative in short exact sequences
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $0\to\mathcal E_1\to\mathcal E_2\to\mathcal E_3\to0$ be a short exact sequence of finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-modules of constant ranks $r_1,r_2,r_3$ respectively, so $r_2=r_1+r_3$. Define $\det(\mathcal E_i)=\bigwedge^{r_i}\mathcal E_i$, with $\det(0)=\mathcal O_X$. There is a canonical isomorphism of invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module] $\det(\mathcal E_2)\cong\det(\mathcal E_1)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\det(\mathcal E_3)$, compatible with restriction to open subsets of $X$.

source.place: Proof of (*), determinant paragraph: local splitting and top exterior powers

proof.text: Apply the local-splitting statement to obtain an open cover of $X$ on which the given short exact sequence identifies with $0\to\mathcal E_1|_{U_a}\to\mathcal E_1|_{U_a}\oplus\mathcal E_3|_{U_a}\to\mathcal E_3|_{U_a}\to0$. Refine this cover using the constant-rank local-freeness trivializations so that both $\mathcal E_1|_{U_a}$ and $\mathcal E_3|_{U_a}$ are free sheaves with bases of $r_1$ and $r_3$ elements. The split module has rank $r_1+r_3$, hence the assumed rank relation gives $r_2=r_1+r_3$.

source.place: Proof of (*), determinant paragraph: local splitting

proof.text: On each refined member $U_a$, apply the top-exterior-power direct-sum isomorphism to the free $\mathcal O_{U_a}$-modules with the chosen bases. The sheaf $\bigwedge^{r_i}(\mathcal E_i|_{U_a})$ is free with basis the wedges of those basis sections, by the free-module exterior-power basis statement, and this identification is compatible with restriction. Thus the module isomorphism gives $\det(\mathcal E_2)|_{U_a}\cong\det(\mathcal E_1)|_{U_a}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{U_a}}\det(\mathcal E_3)|_{U_a}$.

source.place: Proof of (*), determinant paragraph: top exterior powers

proof.text: On $U_a$, for a local splitting $s:\mathcal E_3|_{U_a}\to\mathcal E_2|_{U_a}$ and inclusion $u:\mathcal E_1|_{U_a}\to\mathcal E_2|_{U_a}$, define the map by sending $(a_1\wedge\cdots\wedge a_{r_1})\otimes(b_1\wedge\cdots\wedge b_{r_3})$ to $u(a_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge u(a_{r_1})\wedge s(b_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge s(b_{r_3})$. If $s'$ is another splitting, then $s'(b)-s(b)$ lies in $u(\mathcal E_1|_{U_a})$; expanding the wedge, every term containing an $s'-s$ factor has $r_1+1$ factors from the free rank-$r_1$ module $u(\mathcal E_1|_{U_a})$ and vanishes by [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis]. Hence the map is independent of $s$, so the local maps agree on overlaps and with restriction. They therefore glue to the canonical isomorphism, and when a rank is zero the same formula uses $\bigwedge^0=\mathcal O_X$.

source.place: Proof of (*), determinant paragraph: local splitting and gluing
